In an abandoned pearl-processing factory on the outskirts of Zhuji, China, before dawn, cool blue-silver light filters through cracked industrial windows and falls across three Chinese women standing in a loose triangle on cold concrete. Mei, a slim woman in her late twenties with sharp cheekbones and her dark hair pulled into a sleek low chignon, polished and neat, stands with her back partially to the largest window, her satin slip dress with its floor-length cape shimmering like liquid pearl where the pale light catches the folds. The fabric pools around her bare feet, and her hands clutch a single white orchid stem too tightly, knuckles pale, her gaze fixed on Lin's face with an expression she cannot name as desire. Lin, broad-shouldered and twenty-eight, her loose waves cascading down her back nearly to her waist, stands opposite Mei with her weight on her left foot, her own identical pearl cape draped over one shoulder to reveal more of the slip dress beneath, her lips slightly parted as if she has just begun to speak words of commitment she has rehearsed for weeks. Yun, athletic and twenty-nine, her dark hair woven in a braided crown wrapped around her head like a circlet of rope, stands at the incomplete corner of their triangle, her identical liquid pearl gown still fully closed around her, her arms crossed loosely at her waist, her eyes lowered to the concrete floor where a thin trail of abandoned machinery grease marks a path between the two women she thinks she is only watching. The camera holds them medium-wide, their isolation in the vast derelict space emphasized by the empty steel shelving and broken processing tables receding into shadow behind them, shallow depth of field keeping the texture of the pearl fabric and the uncertainty in Mei's eyes sharp while the factory's ruined depth softens into blue-gray haze, negative space above their heads suggesting the resolution they cannot yet speak.

She wears a cyber couture bridal suit beneath the tulle crown, ivory blazer and wide-leg trousers tailored sharp against the deliberate blur of her head, the contrast deliberate and unsettling.
